# Retail Glossary

- **Shrink** — inventory loss: the difference between recorded (book) and actual counted stock, from theft,
  damage, error, or fraud. Measured as a % of sales.
- **Comp sales / comps** — comparable-store sales: this period's sales vs. the same period a year ago, same stores.
- **UPT** — units per transaction; how many items in the average basket.
- **ADS** — average daily sales.
- **Conversion** — share of store visitors who make a purchase.
- **Planogram (POG)** — the diagram dictating exactly where each product sits on a fixture.
- **Planogram reset / reset** — re-merchandising a section to a new planogram (often seasonal).
- **Endcap** — the display at the end of an aisle; prime real estate, reset seasonally.
- **Facing** — pulling product forward so the front row is full and neat; "facing the store."
- **SKU** — stock-keeping unit; a single sellable item/variant.
- **RTV** — return to vendor; sending defective/discontinued stock back to the supplier for credit.
- **Markdown** — a permanent price reduction to clear inventory (vs. a temporary promo).
- **GMROI** — gross margin return on inventory investment; profit per dollar of inventory.
- **BOPIS** — buy online, pick up in store.
- **Go-backs** — items customers left behind that need returning to their home location.
- **Recovery** — restoring the floor to standard (facing, straightening, refilling) at open/close.
- **Mystery shop** — a paid anonymous shopper who scores the store on service standards.
- **NPS** — Net Promoter Score; a customer-loyalty/satisfaction measure.
- **LP** — Loss Prevention.
- **Till** — a cash register drawer.
- **Zone / zoning** — assigning associates to areas of the floor for coverage.
- **PIP** — Performance Improvement Plan; a formal, documented plan to correct an employee's performance.
